subject: Order Form redline — loss allocation / direct vs. indirect damages
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tr@acme.com>
Date: 2025-12-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form: Limitation of Liability — ACME/Redwood

Karthik,

Thanks for the call this morning. We reviewed the MSA + Order Form and have one remaining ask from procurement on loss allocation. They want the Order Form to (1) carve out loss of profits and loss of goodwill from the cap, and (2) explicitly include data loss and restoration as a recoverable item (their IT team is worried about exposure if customer PII is impacted).

Attached is our redline (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Can you confirm Redwood’s position on:
- Whether lost profits / lost goodwill will be carved out from the monetary cap, or instead treated as excluded consequential damages;
- Whether you can accept a narrow carve-out for verified data loss (they prefer to limit to direct restoration costs and third-party notification costs); and
- A dollar cap that is acceptable so procurement can clear this.

We’re aiming to finalize procurement review by COB Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Head of Procurement
Acme Enterprises

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (document, 1 file)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-15T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Order Form: Limitation of Liability — ACME/Redwood

Aditya / Laura — forwarding Acme’s redline and request. Key asks summarized below. We need legal sign-off on suggested carve-out framing; sales needs a pragmatic counter so procurement can close.

Acme asks:
- Carve out lost profits & lost goodwill from the cap (they want these as recoverable)
- Narrow carve-out for data loss (restore costs + third-party notification)
- Prefer a dollar cap defined at the Order Form level (vs. MSA)

Options I think are commercially reasonable:
A) Keep standard cap = 12x monthly fees (order form revenue) or $1M whichever is greater; expressly carve out only "fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP infringement". Exclude lost profits / goodwill as consequential damages. For data loss, offer a narrow direct-damage category limited to reasonable restoration costs (documented invoices) up to a separate modest cap (suggest $250k).

B) Hybrid compromise: keep cap at 12x fees but add a data-loss bucket: for verified data loss caused by Redwood’s breach of obligations, allow recovery of documented data restoration and notification costs up to the greater of $250k or 100% of the fees paid in prior 12 months. Still exclude lost profits/goodwill.

Below are suggested drafting snippets for the MSA/Order Form (please review /edit):

---- SNIPPET 1 (direct damages definition, conservative) ----
"Direct Damages" means proven damages incurred by Customer that are the natural and proximate result of Supplier’s breach, excluding Consequential Damages. Consequential Damages include, without limitation, loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data (except as expressly provided in the 'Data Restoration' carve-out), loss of use, and loss of goodwill.

---- SNIPPET 2 (data restoration carve-out) ----
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may recover documented and reasonable costs of data restoration and third-party notification incurred as a direct result of Supplier’s material breach of its security obligations, up to an aggregate cap equal to the greater of (i) $250,000 and (ii) the total fees paid by Customer under the Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the incident.

---- SNIPPET 3 (order form cap language) ----
Supplier’s aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Order Form shall not exceed the greater of (i) twelve (12) times the monthly recurring fees paid under this Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability and (ii) $1,000,000, except that the foregoing shall not limit Customer’s ability to recover amounts described in the Data Restoration carve-out above.

Can Legal weigh in on: (1) acceptability of the $250k / 12x hybrid; (2) whether we can accept explicit carve-out for data restoration on a per-order basis; and (3) whether we can insist that lost profits / goodwill are excluded as consequential damages.

I attached a short redline with my markup (RNK_proposed_carveouts_v1.docx).

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RNK_proposed_carveouts_v1.docx (draft language)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-16T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form: Limitation of Liability — ACME/Redwood

Karthik / Aditya — quick thoughts from GTM: procurement will push hard on lost profits; they sometimes get internal approvals if we provide a narrowly‑tailored remedy for data loss plus a modest monetary bucket. Please consider the language below as a near-final counter. Keep it short and prescriptive.

Proposal (sales-preferred):
1) Cap stays at 'greater of 12x monthly fees or $1M' at the Order Form level.
2) Lost profits / loss of goodwill remain excluded as Consequential Damages.
3) Add a narrow Data Restoration carve-out limited to: (a) documented costs to restore or recreate Customer Data; and (b) third-party notification and credit-monitoring costs where required by law, up to the greater of $250,000 or total fees paid in prior 12 months. Recovery requires: (i) mutual forensic review; (ii) written notice within 30 days of discovery; (iii) Customer mitigation obligations.

Suggested concise clause to insert into Order Form: 
"Data Restoration. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Order Form or MSA, if Supplier’s breach of its security obligations causes the loss, corruption or unauthorized disclosure of Customer Data, Supplier’s sole obligation shall be to (i) use commercially reasonable efforts to restore such Customer Data from Supplier’s backups; and (ii) reimburse documented, reasonable and necessary third‑party costs incurred by Customer to restore such Customer Data and to provide legally required notification to affected individuals, in each case up to the greater of $250,000 and the fees paid by Customer under this Order Form in the 12 months preceding the incident. Any recovery under this Section shall be exclusive of Consequential Damages, including lost profits, diminution of goodwill, and loss of business opportunity."

If legal is OK with the forensic/notice gating and the $250k floor, I’m comfortable using this as our counter and pushing procurement to accept. If legal thinks $250k is too low, propose $500k as fallback.

-L
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tr@acme.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-18T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redline — loss allocation / direct vs. indirect damages

Sana — thanks for the redline and patience while we reviewed with Legal. 

Summary and our counter (attached: ACME_OrderForm_v3_counter_redline.docx):
- We will not accept an open carve-out that makes lost profits / loss of goodwill recoverable — those are Consequential Damages and remain excluded.
- We will accept a narrow, conditional Data Restoration carve-out limited to documented restoration costs and required third‑party notification/credit monitoring costs, subject to mutual forensic review and mitigation obligations.
- The Data Restoration bucket will be capped at the greater of $250,000 or the fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months prior to the incident.
- Order Form aggregate cap remains the greater of (i) 12x monthly recurring fees, and (ii) $1,000,000, subject only to the Data Restoration carve‑out above.

If this structure works for Acme, please confirm and we’ll circulate an updated Order Form and DocuSign link for signature. If procurement insists on lost profits / goodwill being recoverable, we will need an executive sponsor to authorize a bespoke exception and will require escalated review (and likely additional commercial consideration).

Proposed next step: Please confirm acceptance of the Data Restoration carve-out language by EOD tomorrow so we can route to procurement. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2025-42.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
